title: Se pasiva / impersonal: la sociedad de castas

sections.content: The se-passive fits classification systems well: people were classified, privileges were granted or denied, a genre became popular — all sustained social practices, not one official's single act. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En la sociedad colonial se clasificaba a las personas según su origen y su ascendencia.
items.english: In colonial society, people were classified according to their origin and ancestry.

items.spanish: Con estas categorías se concedían, o se negaban, ciertos privilegios legales.
items.english: With these categories, certain legal privileges were granted, or denied.

items.spanish: En el siglo dieciocho, se popularizó en Nueva España un género pictórico dedicado a este sistema.
items.english: In the eighteenth century, a pictorial genre devoted to this system became popular in New Spain.

items.spanish: Estas pinturas se encargaban a artistas locales, y se enviaban con frecuencia a España.
items.english: These paintings were commissioned from local artists, and were frequently sent to Spain.

sections.content: Se clasificaba, se concedían, se encargaban — all imperfect tense, because these were ongoing, repeated practices, not single completed events. Watch how the se-passive verb agrees with what follows it: se concedían privilegios (plural verb for plural privilegios), se popularizó un género (singular verb for singular género).
